trigger.symptom: The D~29 rung at warmup 2000 / 500 draws / 4 chains had zero divergences but failed the ESS and R-hat gates (bulk ESS roughly 100, R-hat roughly 1.04; the figures are quoted from sweep_beaker_diag.yaml's header, not re-derived here).
trigger.cause: Unknown at launch. Two hypotheses were under test: trajectories truncated at max_tree_depth (slow mixing with no divergences, cheap to fix) versus genuinely slow mixing (fixed by more draws). The run changes no sampler setting; it only collects the extra NUTS fields (num_steps, energy, accept_prob) that distinguish them.
evidence: Beaker experiment 01M1MQB0SRRBDDRKP1SX3T55DV (the ladder wave that produced the failing D~29 rung)

deviations.record_origin: Written after the fact (2026-10-13) from the job's own Beaker status and entrypoint log, plus the W&B run config. It was not produced by the launcher at submission time.
deviations.submitted_spec_note: The rendered experiment_resumable_submitted.yaml for this submission was lost with scratch space, and the Beaker client in use cannot fetch a submitted spec back. The commits above are the SHAs the container entrypoint reports having checked out, which is stronger evidence of what ran than a spec would be. The exact launched command line is in the job log; its subject_ratio argument was cut off in the log line and is confirmed from the W&B config (0.049).
deviations.commits_reachable_from_main: All three are ancestors of today's main on their repos. The wrapper commit is a feature commit (feat(hb): collect the sampler diagnostics ...), not a merge to main at the time of the run.
deviations._meta_note: _meta describes this record's producer, not the run: its commit fields are the sandbox checkout at write time. The run's own commits are under tasks[0].executed_commits.
